title: Special resolution to change a company's name
ruleSource: Written from S.A Badmus' Corporate Law drafts (Lawdeck knowledge base). To be confirmed by the legal reviewer, including every section of the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020 cited.

parts.why: Company documents carry the company's name, registered address and registration (RC) number, and for resolutions and notices the statutory heading. Source: Corporate Law Practice drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

parts.text: SPECIAL RESOLUTION TO CHANGE THE NAME OF {{oldName}} TO {{newName}} PURSUANT TO SECTION 50(1) OF THE COMPANIES AND ALLIED MATTERS ACT 2020
parts.why: The title of the resolution and the law it is passed under. Source: Corporate Law Practice drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

parts.text:
At the general meeting of the company held on {{meetingDate}} at {{meetingPlace}}, the following resolution was proposed and duly passed as a special resolution:

"That, subject to the consent of the Corporate Affairs Commission, the name of the company be changed from {{oldName}} to {{newName}}."
parts.why: Where and when the meeting was held, and the resolution itself in quotation marks, subject to the Commission's consent. A change of name needs a special resolution of the members. Source: Corporate Law Practice drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

Resolutions are dated and signed, usually by two directors or a director and the secretary. Always sign and date in the exam, on or before the exam date. Source: Corporate Law Practice drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).
